Dear Racing Fan;
It's a tradition that is now a third of a century old, after Indy, it's Milwaukee.
Welcome to the 33rd running of the Rex Mays Classic.
Many people and companies have been working hard to bring you this fine
weekend of racing, including the sponsor of the program, Gould, Inc.; the
sponsor of the Indy Car World Series, PPG Industries; the sponsors of the
Super Vees, Volkswagen of America, Inc. and Robert Bosch Corp.; the
sanctioning bodies, Championship Auto Racing Teams (CART) and the
Sports Car Club of America (SCCA); the Wisconsin Auto Racing Staff; and the
staff of the Wisconsin State Fair Park.
On behalf of them, I hope you have a fine weekend and enjoy the races on the
Milwaukee Mile.
Both the PPG Indy Car World Series and Robert Bosch-VW Super Vees are
scheduled to return for the July 31 and Aug. 1 Provimi Veal/Tony
Bettenhausen Classic. If you don't have tickets for those, order soon, while the
selection is good.
There are also a couple of exciting stock car shows remaining on the 1982
schedule, the July 18 Miller High Life 200 for the American Speed Association
Circuit of Champions and the Aug. 28-29 Milwaukee Sentinel 200 for the Auto
Racing Club of America (ARCA) and United States Auto Club (USAC) cars.
If you have any questions or comments about the events this weekend, I, or
any member of my staff are very interested in hearing them.
Sincerely,
John Kaishian, President

The Gould Rex Mays Classic is an event of special
meaning to defending CART Indy Car World Series titlist
Rick Mears.
Not only is the event sponsored by the same company
which sponsors his Indy Car ride, Gould, Inc., but it was
in the 1978 Rex Mays event that Mears scored his first
win on the circuit.
Mears debuted on the Championship Trail in 1976, star-
ting three events. The following season marked his first
full-time effort on the circuit and he was named the
division's top rookie pilot.
Mears joined the Penske Racing Team in 1978 and
after a 23rd place finish in the Indianapolis 500 enabled
him to claim a share of the event's rookie of the year
award, he posted his initial win in the Rex Mays 150,
even though his car ran out of fuel on the final lap.
He added two more victories to his total in 1978 and
finished ninth in the point standings.
In 1979, Mears won three events, including the In-
dianapolis 500, and posted runnerup finishes in four other
events en route to capturing his first CART cham-
pionship.

GORDON JOHNCOCK, 45, of Coldwater, Mich.,
recorded 10 top 10 finishes in 12 starts en route to
placing third in the 1981 Indy Car World Series
standings. His best showing was a second place finish in
a 500-kilometer event at Riverside Calif. Johncock
paced 29 miles in last year's Gould Rex Mays 150 but
wound up being credited with 16th place when a
gearbox problem sidelined him after 138 laps. He
returned to the Milwaukee Mile in September for the
Bettenhausen 200 and came in sixth after leading five
miles. His most prestigious victories came in the 1973
and 1982 Indianapolis 500s. He won the 1976 National
Driving Championship and is off to a strong start in
CART this year having placed fifth in the Kraco 150 at
Phoenix, Ariz., and second in a 200 mile event at
Hampton, Ga. He drives the STP Oil Treatment Wildcat-
Cosworth.
